title: Not In The Room
narrativeQuestion: How did club owners turn a popular game into an industry, and what changed when the workers were not parties to the rules?

chapters.title: The Mess
chapters.claim: Professional baseball's real instability made durable rules valuable to owners, players, and fans.

chapters.title: February 2, 1876
chapters.claim: A documented New York meeting created the National League; the locked-door detail comes from later memoir.

chapters.title: Read It Like An Accountant
chapters.claim: Four sensible charter clauses all moved control toward existing club owners and league leadership.

chapters.title: Territory Is The Product
chapters.claim: One club per city turned territory into a licensed exclusive right: a franchise.
The reserve agreement removed rival bids from the player labor market even though players were not parties to it.

chapters.title: A Charter Nobody Enforces Is Stationery
chapters.claim: The league became durable because it imposed real costs on members that broke its rules.

chapters.title: What They Refused To Sell
chapters.claim: Beer and Sunday-game restrictions show the league spending revenue to buy legitimacy.

chapters.title: Who Pays For All This
chapters.claim: Programs, subscriptions, and turnstiles made the fan a measured customer.

chapters.title: Higher Pay, Less Freedom
chapters.claim: Compensation and freedom to change employers are different axes, placing reserved players in an unusual position.

chapters.title: The Two Stories That Go Too Far
chapters.claim: Both the greedy-villain story and the natural-market story fail when tested against the documents.

chapters.title: Not In The Room
chapters.claim: By 1880 owners had assembled a durable five-part industry stack without players participating in its governance.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.claim: The terms board attaches business vocabulary to mechanisms already made visible.

chapters.title: Note Repair
chapters.claim: The repair board replaces six common oversimplifications with bounded evidence statements.

accuracyNotes: Professional baseball predated the National League; the narrower claim is that the League made club-owner control durable.
The February 2, 1876 meeting is documented. The locked-door detail comes from later memoir and is labeled that way.
The first 1879 reserve agreement covered only a limited number of players per club and hardened later.
Do not place an exact Cincinnati expulsion year on the student page because accounts compress the 1879 to 1880 sequence differently.
Player wages are described as generally above most industrial wages without using a single unsupported comparison figure.
The lesson claims that the franchise, schedule, enforcement, and labor-control architecture recurs, not that every later league copied every clause.
